dn28:1.19: ‘Sir, I have such confidence in the Buddha that I believe there’s no other ascetic or brahmin—whether past, future, or present—whose direct knowledge is superior to the Buddha when it comes to awakening?’
dn28:2.10: ‘And all the perfected ones, fully awakened Buddhas of the future will give up the five hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom. Their mind will be firmly established in the four kinds of mindfulness meditation. They will correctly develop the seven awakening factors. And they will awaken to the supreme perfect awakening.’
dn28:2.11: And the Blessed One, who is now the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha, gave up the five hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom. His mind was firmly established in the four kinds of mindfulness meditation. He correctly developed the seven awakening factors. And he awakened to the supreme perfect awakening.
dn28:19.7: ‘Reverend Sāriputta, will there be any other ascetic or brahmin in the future whose direct knowledge is superior to the Buddha when it comes to awakening?’ I would tell them ‘No.’
dn28:19.8: ‘Reverend Sāriputta, is there any other ascetic or brahmin at present whose direct knowledge is superior to the Buddha when it comes to awakening?’ I would tell them ‘No.’
dn28:19.11: ‘Reverend Sāriputta, will there be any other ascetic or brahmin in the future whose direct knowledge is equal to the Buddha when it comes to awakening?’ I would tell them ‘Yes.’
